fix_decisions.claim_text: Release note says tool and resource error messages are unchanged, but errors the 2.x SDK raises outside the tool function (argument validation, output conversion) keep the SDK's own text.
fix_decisions.evidence: Deleted the overbroad clause 'tool and resource error messages,' from the fragment (Writing the fix: delete a false clause when no criterion needs it). Criterion 15 states those outside-function errors keep the 2.x SDK text; no criterion requires the release note to claim error text is unchanged. Class sweep: git grep for unchanged-error-text claims outside CHANGELOG.md and the frozen release-notes archive found only this fragment. tests/unit -k changelog: 27 passed.

phase3_findings.description: Registration through _tool/_resource (so every tool and widget gets the error wrapper) is held only by a comment; no test checks every registered tool went through _tool_errors.
_tool and _resource return Any, discarding the ParamSpec typing _tool_errors carries.
No test sends a non-dict, non-None _meta to pin the fail-closed branch of _request_metadata.
Full error text asserted through a real client for four registrations only; a tool added with plain @mcp.tool would pass the surface test.
Wrapping every crash as ToolError means the 2.x SDK logs it at INFO without a traceback.

tools.md 'Tool error text on mcp 2.x' says any other exception reaches the client as the bare 'Error executing tool <name>', omitting the nested UnexpectedToolError case the SDK sends with ': <generic text>'. Capped at Suggestion by the behavior-inert prose cap.
